# Part II. Web Scraping

## Question 1: Scrape a table.

To begin I am uploading the libraries required for scraping a table from Wikipedia. I'll be using rvest for the webscraping, tidyverse for data cleaning and transformations, janitor to clean up the column names, and stringr for string manipulation. The link to the wikitable was saved into an `html` object.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(rvest)
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(stringr)

html <- read_html("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_areas_of_Chicago")
```


```{r}
ca_table <- html |> 
  html_element("table.wikitable") |> #extracting first table from wikipedia page
  html_table() |> 
  clean_names() |> #keep names in lowercase
  select(no, name, population) #keep relevant columns


ca_table <- ca_table[-c(1, 79), ] #remove the rows with repeated info and the citywide totals

ca_table$name <- ca_table$name |> 
  str_remove("\\[\\d+\\]") #removing the brackets from the names list

ca_table$population <- ca_table$population |> 
  str_remove_all(",") #remove commas from the population row then covert to numeric

ca_table$population <- as.numeric(ca_table$population)

nrow(ca_table)
head(ca_table)
```

Then here I am filtering for the single row of West Town and the communities with the highest populations.
```{r}
ca_table |> 
  filter(no == 24)

ca_table |>
  slice_max(order_by = population, n = 5)
```
## Question 2: Scrape with CSS selectors. 

In this section I am scraping a website called 
```{r}
html2 <- read_html("https://books.toscrape.com/") #read the url for scraping and save into object

section <- html2 |> 
  html_elements("li.col-xs-6.col-sm-4.col-md-3.col-lg-3") 
#save the repeating section that contains the info

title <- section |> 
  html_element("h3") |> #extracting the title
  html_text2()

price <-  section |> 
  html_element("p.price_color") |> #extracting each book price
  html_text2()

availability <- section |> 
  html_element("p.instock.availability") |> #extracting the availability
  html_text2()

books <- tibble( #creating a tibble from the previous objects
  title,
  price,
  availability
)

nrow(books)
head(books)

write.csv(books, "books.csv") #saving the table into the documents folder
```
